concepts.title: Displacement Current from Rate of Change of Electric Flux
concepts.definition: The effective electric current inside dielectric media or free space resulting from time-varying electric flux, restoring logical consistency to Ampere circuital law.
concepts.key_idea: A changing electric field produces a magnetic field in the same manner as a conventional electric current.
question_patterns: calculate the displacement current given the rate of change of electric flux
find the displacement current when the electric flux changes at a rate of ...
determine the magnitude of displacement current produced by time-varying electric flux

compute the displacement current inside a capacitor given rate of change of electric flux

solution_steps.action: multiply permittivity of free space by rate of change of electric flux
solution_steps.explain: displacement current equals vacuum permittivity multiplied by time derivative of electric flux

concepts.title: Wavelength of Electromagnetic Wave in Free Space
concepts.definition: The physical spatial length of one complete wave cycle of an electromagnetic wave moving through free space at light speed.
concepts.key_idea: Wavelength varies inversely with frequency for electromagnetic radiation in vacuum.
question_patterns: find the wavelength of an electromagnetic wave given its frequency in vacuum
calculate the wavelength of a wave propagating with frequency ...

solution_steps.action: divide speed of light by wave frequency
solution_steps.explain: wavelength is calculated by dividing speed of light in vacuum by frequency

concepts.title: Frequency of Electromagnetic Wave in Free Space
concepts.definition: The temporal repetition rate of electric and magnetic field oscillations in an electromagnetic wave travelling through vacuum.
concepts.key_idea: Frequency is inversely proportional to wavelength as speed of propagation in vacuum is constant.
question_patterns: calculate the frequency of an electromagnetic wave given its wavelength
find the frequency corresponding to a wavelength of ...

solution_steps.action: divide speed of light by wavelength
solution_steps.explain: frequency is determined by dividing light speed in vacuum by wavelength

concepts.title: Electric Field Amplitude from Magnetic Field Amplitude
concepts.definition: The peak amplitude of the oscillating electric field vector in an electromagnetic wave, derived from magnetic field amplitude.
concepts.key_idea: Electric field amplitude is scaled from magnetic field amplitude by speed of light.
question_patterns: calculate the electric field amplitude given magnetic field amplitude

solution_steps.action: multiply magnetic field amplitude by speed of light
solution_steps.explain: electric field peak equals magnetic field peak multiplied by propagation speed

concepts.title: Magnetic Field Amplitude from Electric Field Amplitude
concepts.definition: The peak amplitude of the oscillating magnetic field vector in an electromagnetic wave, derived from electric field amplitude.
concepts.key_idea: Magnetic field amplitude is electric field amplitude divided by light speed.
question_patterns: calculate the magnetic field amplitude given electric field amplitude
find the amplitude of oscillating magnetic field for electric field amplitude ...
determine the magnetic field vector magnitude given peak electric field ...
what is the magnetic field amplitude when electric field amplitude is ...
compute magnetic field amplitude from electric field amplitude in free space

solution_steps.action: divide electric field amplitude by speed of light
solution_steps.explain: magnetic field peak equals electric field peak divided by propagation speed

concepts.title: Wave Vector and Spatial Frequency of EM Wave
concepts.definition: The propagation constant representing phase change per unit distance along wave propagation vector.
concepts.key_idea: Wave vector magnitude describes spatial variation rate of electromagnetic wave phase.

concepts.title: Speed of Light in Material Medium
concepts.definition: The propagation velocity of electromagnetic disturbance within a physical medium defined by medium permeability and permittivity.
concepts.key_idea: Electromagnetic wave speed decreases inside material media based on electrical and magnetic properties.
question_patterns: calculate the speed of light in a material medium with given permeability and permittivity

solution_steps.explain: multiply magnetic permeability by electric permittivity of medium

solution_steps.action: take reciprocal of square root of product
solution_steps.explain: wave velocity equals inverse square root of medium property product

concepts.title: Maxwell Equations in Free Space
concepts.definition: The set of four mathematical relationships coupling electric charges, currents, and time-varying field distributions.
concepts.key_idea: Complete unification of electrostatics, magnetism, and wave optics.
question_patterns: list Maxwell equations in free space
explain the role of Maxwell equations in predicting electromagnetic waves
state Faraday law and Ampere Maxwell law in field form
what are the four fundamental equations of electromagnetism
verify how Maxwell equations establish symmetry between electric and magnetic fields

solution_steps.explain: surface integral of electric field over closed boundary equals enclosed charge divided by free space permittivity
surface integral of magnetic field over any closed surface is zero reflecting lack of magnetic monopoles
line integral of electric field along closed contour equals negative rate of change of magnetic flux
line integral of magnetic field depends on both conduction current and displacement current

concepts.title: Sources and Transverse Nature of Electromagnetic Waves
concepts.definition: The origin of radiated electromagnetic energy from accelerated charges and mutually orthogonal orientations of field oscillations.
concepts.formula: E_x = E0 * sin(k*z - omega*t), B_y = B0 * sin(k*z - omega*t)
concepts.key_idea: Accelerating charges radiate waves where electric field, magnetic field, and wave vector are mutually perpendicular.
question_patterns: explain how accelerated charges radiate electromagnetic waves
describe the orientation of electric field magnetic field and propagation vector in em waves
why are stationary charges unable to produce electromagnetic waves
show that electric and magnetic field vectors are mutually perpendicular in em waves
verify the transverse nature of plane electromagnetic waves

solution_steps.explain: static charges create electrostatic fields and constant currents create steady magnetic fields, but accelerating charges generate self-sustaining propagating field waves
electric field vector and magnetic field vector oscillate perpendicular to each other and perpendicular to wave propagation direction

concepts.title: Electromagnetic Spectrum Regions and Applications
concepts.definition: The continuous distribution of electromagnetic waves grouped into distinct frequency and wavelength bands.
concepts.key_idea: Electromagnetic spectral regions differ in production mechanisms, detection instruments, and practical applications.
question_patterns: classify different bands of the electromagnetic spectrum
state production and detection methods for microwaves and infrared waves
explain applications of ultraviolet radiation and X rays
what are the main bands of the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing frequency
compare radio waves microwaves and gamma rays by wavelength and generation mechanism

solution_steps.explain: radio waves have longest wavelengths, followed by microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays
radio waves are generated by accelerating electrons in aerials and detected by aerials, whereas gamma rays are produced in nuclear reactions
